A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CogNav, and their text, equations, tables and figures support reliable comparison. v3 includes supplementary material absent from the supplied v2 PDF; additions below refer to documented content, without assuming when the underlying work was performed.

before.justification: v2 reports original navigation results on HM3D, MP3D and RoboTHOR, state and prompt ablations, and simulated and real-robot navigation examples.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and additionally reports model substitutions, category-level comparisons, failure analysis, component timings and navigation examples in its supplement.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithm 1 retain the same heterogeneous cognitive map, landmark prompting, five cognitive states, LLM scheduling and FMM navigation. The supplement presents voxel representation, instance fusion and landmark construction as implementation details of this pipeline, rather than establishing a revised method.

E1.justification: Both versions cover indoor object-goal navigation on HM3D, MP3D and RoboTHOR and describe the same two robot platforms. The supplement adds category breakdowns and examples within this coverage, without establishing a new dataset, task or distinct environmental test regime.

E2.justification: CoW becomes a scored comparator in the supplemental MP3D category comparison, alongside ESC and SG-Nav (Figure 2). v2 cites the same work as CoWs but reports no corresponding scores. Main-text comparator membership remains unchanged.

E3.justification: Supplementary Table 2 adds controlled substitutions using Llama3.1-8B-Instruct and Cogvlm2-llama3-chat-19B. Section 2.3 introduces per-component timing and execution-frequency measurements including failed episodes. Main benchmark settings remain unchanged; the separately reported 277/1008 failure analysis does not establish a revision to the main validation split.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained state and prompt ablations, v3 adds LLM/VLM sensitivity testing, component runtime profiling, quantitative failure attribution, a sofa/bed misclassification case and detailed navigation walkthroughs. These substantially expand examination of model dependence, computational bottlenecks and failure mechanisms.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, variability estimates or significance tests. The added percentages and average timings remain point estimates and introduce no uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Main Tables 1–4 retain their values, including CogNav success rates of 72.5%, 46.6% and 54.6% across the three benchmarks. New results include alternate-model HM3D success rates of 62.6%, 64.1% and 69.4%, MP3D category comparisons, failure shares of 35.7% detection failures and 64.3% target inaccessibility, component timings and qualitative trajectories. These are additional results, not improved scores under the original settings.

T1.justification: Supplementary Sections 1.2–1.4 add explicit definitions of landmark-instance mapping, state-dependent candidate sets and an argmin rule for selecting the final target landmark. This makes the mathematical specification more precise; the original equations remain unchanged and no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: LLM-driven cognitive-state modeling, an online correctable heterogeneous map and superior benchmark success rates. The supplementary evidence does not redefine these core claims.

C2.justification: The supplement adds viewpoint-based explanations of category failures, inaccessible targets as a failure source, and scene-graph updating as the principal runtime bottleneck. Existing limitations remain. Its assertion of categorywise superiority except for fireplace and picture overstates Figure 2, which also shows SG-Nav ahead for categories such as towel and table.

D1.justification: v2 defers substantial technical information to supplementary material unavailable in that PDF. v3 supplies voxel and SoM fusion details, Voronoi reduction and landmark rules, worked prompts, model identifiers, component timings, and robot hardware and ROS configuration, including the RTX 3090Ti workstation. This substantially expands implementation and reproducibility documentation.

R1.justification: The main related-work discussion and 48 references are retained. The supplement adds Llama 3, CogVLM2 and three hardware references, and explains more specific differences from ConceptGraphs instance fusion and VoroNav graph construction.

P1.justification: The main prose and section sequence are essentially unchanged. v3 adds a separately organized technical-details and experiments supplement, explanatory expansions, acknowledgements, and a joint-first-author marker for Zhinan Yu, without broadly rewriting the main narrative.

P2.justification: v3 retains the main displays and adds three supplementary tables and nine figures, including notation, model comparisons, timings, an MP3D bar chart, fusion and verification examples, full prompt displays and a multi-page navigation walkthrough. These substantially expand the visual explanation and presentation of evidence.

improvement.justification: The supplement improves transparency through concrete construction rules, prompt examples and robot specifications, while model-sensitivity and failure analyses strengthen scrutiny of the unchanged main results. These benefits are tempered by overstated MP3D categorywise superiority and inconsistent timing dataset/model descriptions in supplementary Table 3 and its surrounding text. The additions therefore support a modest net improvement.
